bio.summary: Fuqua previously served on the Boulder Valley school board and is now seeking a council seat. He prioritizes affordable family housing, climate resilience and government transparency.
bio.public_office: Boulder Valley School District board member

statements.text: Continue to improve efforts to make the city budget accessible and understandable for residents.
statements.speaker: Sam Fuqua

statements.text: I’m not convinced at this point that the DDA is the right tool.
statements.speaker: Sam Fuqua

statements.text: I am open to reconsidering the DDA because there is some evidence of its effectiveness in strengthening downtowns elsewhere.
statements.speaker: Sam Fuqua
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Sam Fuqua

statements.text: Fuqua said he would have voted against sending the DDA proposal to DDA voters had he been on Council for the mid-2026 vote.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Sam Fuqua’s interview

statements.text: I am committed not only to making myself available to meet with business owners on a regular basis, but also to proactively seeking them out to listen to their input, ask questions (that probably lead to more questions), explain my positions and also sometimes change my mind based on new information.
statements.speaker: Sam Fuqua
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Sam Fuqua

statements.text: Fuqua also wants the partner developers and agencies to build market-rate, middle-income housing on city-owned land.
statements.speaker: Daily Camera reporter (reporting Sam Fuqua)

statements.text: Businesses should expect the City to enforce ordinances and preserve public safety in all commercial and residential districts but we should target our resources where we have the biggest challenges, including Downtown and on The Hill .
statements.speaker: Sam Fuqua
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Sam Fuqua
